# ProjectDeck

> Local project catalog and control deck for AI-built projects. Scans your dev folders, discovers runnable projects, and gives you one local web UI to inspect, start, stop, and watch logs.

ProjectDeck is a local-only web application (Node.js + React) for developers who accumulate dozens of AI-generated repositories across Node, Python, Go, Rust, Java, Swift, Android, Electron, uni-app, and Docker. It solves three problems: not knowing which projects exist, not remembering what each one is, and not having one place to start/stop them.

## What it solves

- **Discovery**: scans configured roots and nested repositories; finds services, desktop apps, mini programs, and mobile projects.
- **Understanding**: detects tech stack, reads README, shows path, version, git branch, last commit, build artifacts, and creation date.
- **Control**: starts and stops projects from the browser, with real-time streaming logs (SSE + ANSI colors) and accurate running state based on port ownership, not just open ports.

## Core features (v0.0.2)

- Zero-config scan of `~/Code` (configurable roots, depth, ignore list)
- Only runnable projects are indexed; docs-only and pure packages are filtered with reasons
- Scan report modal: roots, rules, scanned directory count, filtered items, errors, duration
- Backend-style layout: sidebar + dashboard + project list + detail page
- One-click start / stop / restart for projects with a start command
- Startup failures are classified instead of reported as success: `port-in-use`, `missing-deps`, `missing-script`, `missing-runtime`, `permission`
- Dependency preflight: `node_modules` missing while `package.json` declares deps is flagged, with a one-click `npm/pnpm/yarn/bun install` whose output streams to the terminal
- Live terminal view with ANSI colors, auto-scroll, pause, and clear
- Port ownership check via `lsof` so a port used by another project does not mark this one running
- Observed ports: every response re-reads the listener map and attributes each port to the deepest matching project, so ports hardcoded in source (e.g. 8365 in tools/dev.js) show up and plugin ports never get stolen by the monorepo
- Stable port proxy: auto-assign (9100–9199) or type a fixed port per project; ProjectDeck forwards it to the project's current real port, so frpc / reverse proxy config does not change when the dev server hops ports. Multi-port projects can pin the target (e.g. web 5173 instead of API 3000). Mappings persist in `config.json` under `stablePorts`, keyed by project id with name/path for re-matching
- Sortable list view with creation date and last operation
- Local HTTP API and hash routes (`#/dashboard`, `#/projects`, `#/project/:id`, `#/settings`)
- Automated tests: `npm test` (unit + API integration with fixtures, SSE, process-group stop) and `npm run test:e2e` (real browser: start → logs → stop → failure banner → i18n)

## Quick start

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npm start
# open http://127.0.0.1:4321
```

Development:

```bash
npm run dev
# API 4321, Vite 5310
```

Options:

```bash
projectdeck --root ~/Code --root ~/Work --port 4400 --no-open
projectdeck --all   # also show docs-only and package projects
```

## How scanning works

1. Walk each root up to `maxDepth`.
2. Detect project markers: `package.json`, `manifest.json` + `pages.json`, `*.xcodeproj`, `Package.swift`, `AndroidManifest.xml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, `pom.xml`, `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `compose.yaml`.
3. Index only projects that can run: have a start command, or are desktop/mini-program/mobile projects.
4. Skip `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, `uni_modules`, `sdk`, `HBuilder-*`, `Android-SDK*`, `examples`, and similar.
5. Stop descending after a project is identified, except into `plugins/`.

## Start / stop / logs

- Start uses the detected entry command, e.g. `npm run dev`, `python3 app.py`, `go run .`.
- Each project runs in its own process group so stopping kills the whole tree (npm → vite → node).
- stdout/stderr are captured, kept in a ring buffer, written to `~/.projectdeck/logs/<id>.log`, and streamed to the UI over SSE.
- Running state is verified by matching the listening port to the process working directory.

## Configuration

`~/.projectdeck/config.json`

```json
{
  "port": 4321,
  "host": "127.0.0.1",
  "roots": ["/Users/you/Code"],
  "maxDepth": 6,
  "ignore": ["my-vendor-dir"]
}
```

Runtime state: `~/.projectdeck/runtime.json`
Logs: `~/.projectdeck/logs/<project-id>.log`

## API

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/projects` | Project list with runtime state |
| POST | `/api/scan` | Rescan and return a report |
| GET | `/api/projects/:id` | Project detail + README |
| POST | `/api/projects/:id/start` | Start |
| POST | `/api/projects/:id/stop` | Stop |
| POST | `/api/projects/:id/restart` | Restart |
| POST | `/api/projects/:id/install` | Install dependencies (streams into the log) |
| PUT | `/api/projects/:id/stable-port` | Set or clear a stable port (`{"port": 9100}` / `{"port": null}`) |
| GET | `/api/projects/:id/logs` | Recent logs |
| GET | `/api/projects/:id/logs/stream` | SSE log stream |
| GET | `/api/runtime` | Runtime states |
| GET | `/api/config` | Current config |

## Status

Early alpha. Implemented: scan, catalog, dashboard, list, detail, start/stop/restart, live logs, scan report.
Planned: MCP server (stdio + HTTP), GitHub import, FRP read-only panel, pm2/Docker drivers, Tauri desktop shell.

local project manager, developer dashboard, process manager, dev server manager, project catalog, AI-generated projects, pm2 alternative, start stop restart, live logs, SSE, self-hosted, local-first, macOS, TypeScript, React, Fastify.
